title: Console: MVP 'Insight Cards' + cost baseline — scope reduction and acceptance
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need to trim the Console observability scope to land an actionable MVP for Q2 that gives product and platform teams quick, high-signal visibility into latency, cost direction, and reliability without building full dashboards, a detailed trace explorer, or per-token cost breakdown. This ticket defines the reduced-scope 'Insight Cards' surface plus a lightweight cost baseline and the acceptance criteria for ship.

Background and rationale:
- Prior scope included full per-route dashboards, an interactive trace viewer, long-retention cost hierarchies, and token-level cost decomposition. That scope is high effort and adds delays.
- We must deliver useful metrics quickly to validate that customers get value from observable cost/latency signals before investing in a deeper surface.
- Users (internal platform, early enterprise customers) have repeatedly asked for fast indicators of regressions and rough cost trends. 'Insight Cards' are a card-based, low-friction UI to surface top signals.

Goals for this slice (MVP):
1) Ship 3 Insight Cards on the Console home for projects:
   - Latency card (p50/p95/p99) across selected time windows (1h/24h/7d).
   - Cost baseline card (estimated $/k tokens and 7d trend) per project — coarse-grained, rounded to nearest cent.
   - Reliability card (error rate and failed requests count) with simple top-3 error buckets.
2) Provide a minimal backend metrics API that aggregates telemetry on 1-minute buckets and supports the cards.
3) Implement simple trace sampling indicator (not a full trace explorer): a sampled-trace rate metric and a link that exports a sample to a log/PR for SRE debugging.
4) Access control: only users with project 'viewer' can see cards; admin can opt-in to show cost for their org.

Non-goals (explicit cuts):
- No interactive drilldown dashboards or custom time-series editors.
- No token-level cost decomposition (per-token classifier). Cost will be an approximate $/k tokens projection derived from route averages and model cost profiles.
- No full trace UI (span timeline, flamegraphs). We'll surface a sampled-trace link to logs/GH issue template.
- No historical retention beyond 90 days for the MVP; long-term retention postponed.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Backend team will reuse the existing metrics ingestion pipeline but add an aggregation layer (1m buckets). We will prefer approximate aggregation to avoid expensive joins.
- Cost baseline uses model-profile mapping maintained in runtime-1.18 release; if a runtime change affects model names, we fallback to a conservative estimate.
- UI will be responsive and built from a single reusable Card component (Design to provide token and spacing constraints).

Trade-offs discussed:
- Accuracy vs speed: we accept +/-10-20% variance in cost estimate to avoid high-latency joins and storage costs.
- Traces: shipping a sampled-trace counter + link provides actionable signal without building the trace viewer. If customers need deeper traces, we'll follow up under a separate ticket.
- Retention: 90 days is a pragmatic cut to reduce storage and indexing costs for the MVP.

Links and artifacts:
- PRD (long): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Insight+Cards+PRD (internal)
- Design frames: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/insight-cards-designs
- Backend design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/metrics-aggregation-proposal
- Example GH prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1892 (backend stub + UI mocks)
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Insight Cards show and refresh for a sample project and reflect p50/p95/p99 latency for 1h/24h/7d; displayed values match backend aggregated metrics within tolerance.
AC2: Cost baselined on $/k tokens is displayed on the Cost card with 7d sparkline; cost numbers are human-readable (rounded) and labeled as 'estimate'.
AC3: Reliability card displays error rate and failed requests count, and lists top-3 error buckets (by count) when present.

AC4: Trace sampling indicator shows sample rate (e.g., 1/1000) and a 'Send sample' action that creates a draft GitHub issue with attached exported trace JSON for SRE triage (link must prefill title + labels).
AC5: Role-based visibility enforced: viewer role sees cards; cost card hidden unless org-level billing opt-in is enabled.
AC6: Data latency: cards reflect data within 90s of ingestion for the 1m aggregation window; end-to-end tests validate freshness target.

AC7: Performance: rendering 10 cards for a user (across multiple projects) does not cause >3s initial paint on corporate network; backend queries must respond <500ms for aggregated endpoints under normal load.
AC8: Monitoring: rollout includes a canary at 10% of orgs for 72h with alerting if p95 latency of metrics endpoints >1s or error rate increases by >2x baseline.
AC9: Documentation: Console help page updated with 'Insight Cards' description, cost estimation methodology, and known limitations before GA toggle.
AC10: Security: no PII or full request payloads are exposed via the Cost/Insight cards; exported trace JSON must be sanitized by the backend (no user text).
